With identity_config/profile the operating system must lie inside the class (422 device_identity_mismatch). Omit identity_config entirely to draw a population identity for the requested engine. reuse_identity_seed (returning visitor): send back the `reuse_identity_seed` value a previous create from YOUR org returned to get the same device again; it is scoped to your organization server-side (another org sending the same value gets an unrelated device). identity_id is NOT a replay handle; a non-integer value is ignored (fresh device).

ErrorCode.description: Stable, machine-readable error code. The same vocabulary is used across every endpoint and every SDK. Codes are grouped into two channels: codes returned on a non-2xx response (a problem on our side) and codes returned inside a 200 response body (a problem reaching the target).

ResultError.description: Present inside a 200 response when the request ran but the target site could not be retrieved successfully (an HTTP error from the site, a site block, a CAPTCHA, an unreachable host, or no extractable content). The result also carries `ok: false`.

retryable.description: Whether retrying could succeed. For a blocked page or CAPTCHA this is `true` and means retry with a different identity; for a definitive client error from the site it is `false`.

target_status.description: The HTTP status the target site returned, when known (for example `404` or `503`).

reason.description: An optional sub-reason giving more detail (for example a connection or name-resolution failure when the host could not be reached).

apiKeyHeader.description: Alternative to Authorization: Bearer, send the same GhostCrawl API key as X-Api-Key: gck_YOUR_KEY_HERE. Both transports are accepted by the runtime; when both are supplied, Authorization takes precedence and X-Api-Key is ignored. An internal administrative credential, not available to API customers, also takes precedence.
apiKeyHeader.name: X-Api-Key

bearerAuth.description: Paste your API key as: Authorization: Bearer gck_YOUR_KEY_HERE

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or a parameter was invalid.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication is required: the API key is missing or invalid.

PaymentRequired.description: A usage or spend limit was reached.

Forbidden.description: The API key does not have permission for this action.

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found.

RateLimited.description: The rate limit was exceeded. Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then retry.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable (capacity, a transient render fault, or a busy page). Retryable: back off and retry.

GatewayTimeout.description: The request was not completed in time. Retryable: back off and retry.

InternalError.description: An unexpected error occurred on our side.

post.description: BETA / opt-in. The REST agent lane is disabled by default and returns 404 until enabled for your account/deployment (see the 404 response below). The agent capability is generally available via the MCP `ghostcrawl_agent` tool; this REST surface is still stabilising. Contact support to enable it.

parameters.description: Optional idempotency key (8-256 ASCII printable characters). Supply a fresh UUID or ULID per logically distinct request. Replaying the same request with the same key returns the cached response without re-execution; the same key with a different body is rejected.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

200.description: The agent task completed. The envelope carries the executed step trace, any extracted data, and an engine fidelity receipt.

400.description: Task policy failed, task URL failed gateway policy, proxy failed policy, or tenant/workspace proxy constraint

404.description: Returned when the agent capability is not enabled for this account or deployment. The agent lane runs server-side orchestration, the navigate / act / observe steps execute on GhostCrawl's managed browsers, and calls your bring-your-own (BYO) LLM for the reasoning step using the `provider_config` object in the request body (`base_url`, `api_key`, `model`). Tenant and workspace are derived from your authenticated credentials, never from request fields. While the capability is not enabled the route returns 404; once enabled it returns the agent execution envelope. The BYO LLM is the only part you supply, the orchestration itself is hosted.

429.description: Either capacity exhausted (Retry-After header present, CapacityExhausted429 body) or per-session max_total_llm_calls budget exceeded (X-Ghostcrawl-Warning: budget-exceeded).

503.description: Startup config-preflight gate blocked request handling

post.summary: Start agent lane request (beta, opt-in; 404 until enabled for your account)

post.description: Capture a single JPEG frame from a live browser session. Purpose: grab a still image of a running, interactive session for a live-view preview. Authentication: supply your API key as Authorization: Bearer or via the X-Api-Key header. Parameters: `session_id` (required) identifies the live session; `quality` (optional, 1-100, default 60) sets JPEG quality. Request: POST /v1/cdp/frame with a JSON body such as {"session_id": "sess_123", "quality": 60}. Success: 200 with {"format": "jpeg", "data": "<base64-jpeg>", "engine": "chrome", "width": 1280, "height": 720}. Errors: 401 for missing credentials, 403 when live view is not enabled for your plan or access has been revoked, 404 when the session is not found, and 502 if the frame could not be captured. post.description: structured extraction: deterministic (no model) or connect-your-model. GhostCrawl fetches and renders the URL and reads structured data from the page. For fields that are not present as structured data, connect your own AI provider by passing `model_provider` and its credentials; your connected model then performs the semantic extraction. CONNECT-YOUR-AI (a prompt but NO model_provider): returns 422 model_provider_required, connect your AI/LLM (pass model_provider) to run semantic extraction. Never a silent empty. DETERMINISTIC (model_provider absent, default): 1. The schema is validated (input guard). 2. The URL is validated against private/loopback/metadata targets. 3. The page is fetched and rendered. 4. Structured data is read natively from the page's schema.org JSON-LD / microdata / Open Graph. 5. The result is validated against the schema, 422 on mismatch (field path only). Returns {"url","data","token_estimate"}. When the page embedded NO matching structured data (every field null/empty), the response also carries a non-fatal "warnings":["no_structured_data: …pass model_provider…"] so an all-null 200 is not mistaken for a failure. BRING-YOUR-OWN-MODEL (model_provider present): 1. Target URLs are resolved (urls or [url]). 2. The schema is validated if present. 3. At least one of prompt or schema is required, 400 prompt_or_schema_required otherwise. 4. Model credentials are validated, 400 invalid_model_provider on error (the message never echoes the key). 5. Every target URL is validated before fetching, 400 ssrf_blocked. 6. Each URL is fetched and converted to clean Markdown. 7. Your connected model performs the extraction. 8. With a schema present, the result is validated, 422 on mismatch. Returns {"urls","data","token_estimate"}. Security: 401 without a valid Bearer token. - model_provider.api_key is request-scoped: never persisted, logged, or echoed. - Error responses never echo the schema body, fetched content, or credentials.

get.description: List storage states with cursor pagination. Purpose: retrieve the saved browser storage states in your account, newest first. Authentication: supply your API key as Authorization: Bearer or via the X-Api-Key header. Parameters: `limit` (optional, default 20) sets page size; `cursor` (optional) continues a previous page. Request: GET /v1/storage-states?limit=20. Success: 200 with a cursor-paginated page whose items are storage-state metadata objects (id, name, cookie_count, origins_count, blob_bytes, created_at, updated_at). Errors: 401 for missing credentials, 403 if your key lacks read permission, and 404 when a requested storage state does not exist. Billing: listing is free and counts as a read request. Limits: page size is capped; cursors are opaque. Data and privacy: this read-only operation returns metadata only, the encrypted cookie blob is never included. See the Privacy Policy and Cookie Notice.
get.summary: List storage states with cursor pagination

post.description: snapshot browser storage state from a live session. Captures the current cookies, localStorage, and session storage from the named active profile and saves it encrypted under the given name. Returns storage state metadata on success (credentials are never returned). Storage blobs over 5 MB return storage_state_too_large (400). Pass ``session_id`` to capture from a live cloud session; on a self-hosted deployment ``profile_id`` alone captures from the local active page.
post.summary: Save storage state from live session

post.description: clear profile sticky-attach binding. Removes the storage state binding from a profile so subsequent sessions start without a pre-loaded storage state. Returns 204.

404.description: No active binding found for this profile

delete.description: cascade binding via. Returns 204 on success, 404 (storage_state_not_found) on miss.

get.description: metadata only.

post.description: attach a storage state to a profile. Decrypts and validates the named storage state, filters expired cookies, then sets the sticky binding so subsequent sessions on this profile start with the saved state loaded. Corrupted data → storage_state_decrypt_failed (400).

get.description: List webhooks with cursor pagination. Purpose: retrieve the webhook endpoints registered in your account. Authentication: supply your API key as Authorization: Bearer or via the X-Api-Key header. Parameters: `limit` (optional, default 20) sets page size; `cursor` (optional) continues a previous page. On the initial request omit the cursor; when a next_cursor is returned, pass it as `cursor` to fetch the following page. Errors: 401 for missing credentials and 403 if your key is not entitled to use a restricted filter (that filtered view is available only to keys with the corresponding permission). Success: 200 with {"items": [.], "next_cursor": "<opaque>", "total": 3}, where each item is a webhook object with id, url, and event list; secrets are never returned. Billing: listing is free and counts as a read request. Limits: page size is capped; next_cursor may be empty on the last page. Data and privacy: this read-only operation returns webhook configuration from your own account; webhook secrets are never included. See the Privacy Policy and Cookie Notice.

post.description: Create a new webhook subscription. Returns the webhook plus the plaintext signing secret once. Store the secret immediately, it cannot be recovered; only rotation via /rotate-secret provides a new one.

get.description: Secret: NOT returned.
GET /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries.

post.description: POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/retry. Re-enqueues the failed delivery with a fresh delivery_id; the original event_id is preserved so downstream consumers can detect the retry.
POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/rotate-secret. Generate a new signing secret for the webhook. The previous secret remains valid for a short grace period so in-flight deliveries can still be verified.
post.summary: Rotate webhook signing secret (previous secret valid during grace period).
